name: Kapahulu Market
note: The Honolulu Zoo unveiled Kapahulu Market, its new food and beverage facility, in late August 2022, replacing the zoo's original 1951 concession.

name: Monkeypod Kitchen
note: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman opened on July 14, 2023 at the Outrigger Reef Waikiki Beach Resort, 2169 Kalia Road.

name: La Mer
note: French restaurant at the Halekulani hotel; it opened simultaneously with the rebuilt hotel's grand opening in March 1984. Hawaii's longest-running AAA Five Diamond restaurant, since 1990.

name: Eggs 'n Things
note: Flagship restaurant of the Waikiki breakfast chain; the Saratoga Road restaurant opened March 10, 2009. The brand began on Ena Road in 1974 and the Saratoga site is the third location of the original restaurant. Note: the other Waikiki location, the Waikiki Beach Eggspress at 2464 Kalakaua Ave (opened 2011), was submitted in an earlier run; one travel guide lists this address as 339 Saratoga Road,

name: Heavenly Island Lifestyle
note: All-day restaurant inside Shoreline Hotel Waikiki serving locally sourced island dishes; first welcomed guests in September 2014.

name: Kai Coffee
note: Kai Coffee Hawaii kiosk on the ground floor of Waikiki Shopping Plaza; the plaza's directory listing for it was published in September 2023 and its October 2023 'What's New to Eat' page calls it the brand's newest location.

name: Rivals Waikiki
note: Vegas-inspired sports bar and UltraLounge in the Waikiki Malia Hotel, listed as operating since 2011.

name: Crystal Nail Salon
note: Nail salon in the Waikiki Marketplace at 2310 Kuhio Ave, specializing in manicures and pedicures; established in 2006.

name: Moose McGillycuddy's Pub & Cafe Waikiki
note: Waikiki branch of the Moose McGillycuddy's pub and restaurant chain, opened on Lewers Street in 1980. It was boarded up during the 2020 pandemic and later listed as permanently closed, and Tropics Island Grill & Ale House soft-opened at the address in October 2026.

name: Hyatt Regency Waikiki Farmers Market
note: Indoor farmers market in the Pualeilani Atrium Shops on the Hyatt Regency Waikiki's ground floor, begun in November 2013 as a Thursday evening market. It later moved to other weekday evenings.

name: Starbucks Reserve
note: Starbucks in the former Waikiki Trade Center at Kuhio and Seaside avenues, reportedly open since 2000. In 2017 it added Hawaii's first Starbucks Reserve coffee bar, decorated with island-inspired designs and a mural by a local artist.

name: Morimoto Asia Waikiki
note: Pan-Asian restaurant by Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto and the signature restaurant of the 'Alohilani Resort Waikiki Beach. It opened to the public on February 15, 2018.

name: Mai Tai Bar
note: Beachfront bar at the Royal Hawaiian Hotel, dated to around 1953, when Trader Vic Bergeron created the hotel's Royal Mai Tai using orange and pineapple juice. Bergeron had invented the original Mai Tai in 1944.

name: Kuhio Beach Hula Mound
note: An open-air hula mound on Kuhio Beach across from the Hyatt Regency, built in the city's first phase of Kuhio Beach improvements. The new beach park was blessed in August 2000 and the mound opened with a concert, and the free Kuhio Beach Hula Show is performed there.

name: KONA Coffee Purveyors
note: Flagship cafe of Kona Coffee Purveyors at International Market Place, which opened with the mall's grand opening in August 2016; the roasting company itself was founded in 2008.

name: Maui Brewing Company
note: Brewpub and restaurant on the second floor of the Waikiki Beachcomber hotel, opened January 31, 2017 as Maui Brewing's first Oahu location.

name: Kai Coffee Hawaii
note: The coffee shop's first location, in the Pualeilani Atrium Shops on the ground floor of the Hyatt Regency Waikiki. It opened on May 15, 2014.

name: Blue Ocean Seafood & Steak
note: Seafood and steak food truck in a converted shipping container at 2449 Kuhio Avenue, in business since 2012.

name: Búho Cocina y Cantina
note: Búho Cocina y Cantina is a rooftop Mexican restaurant and bar atop Waikiki Shopping Plaza, open since 2014.

name: Boardriders
note: 7,000-square-foot flagship surf retail store steps from the Duke Kahanamoku statue; reopened in early 2026 after previous closures.

name: MCM
note: Boutique of the luxury leather goods brand MCM on the first level (Queen's Court) of the International Market Place. It opened around 2019 as part of the brand's U.S. expansion.

name: Michael Kors
note: Michael Kors opened its boutique at the renovated International Market Place (2330 Kalakaua Ave, Suite 186) in Waikiki when the center opened in August 2016.

name: American Wagyu Eatery
note: Giftly reports the eatery opened in June 2022. ALOCO identifies its Waikiki food truck at 2525 Cartwright Rd.

name: Double Fat Ice Cream
note: Hawaii News Now says Double Fat Ice Cream was established in Hawaii in 2021 and located behind the Alohilani Resort. Honolulu Magazine identifies its location as the resort at 124 Kealohilani Ave.

name: Queensbreak Restaurant
note: The resort announced completion of its renovation in August 2021, including the new Queensbreak outdoor restaurant. Queensbreak lists its address as 2552 Kalakaua Ave.

name: Honolulu Cookie Company
note: Shop of the Hawaii-based shortbread cookie maker in the rebuilt International Market Place (Space 162). It opened around the time the center reopened in 2016.

name: Edge of Waikiki
note: Oceanfront bar beside the adults-only Infinity Edge Pool at the Sheraton Waikiki, with views toward Diamond Head. The pool and bar were part of a hotel renovation and opened in fall 2009.

name: Honolulu Coffee
note: Kona coffee cafe and kiosk of the Honolulu-based roaster at the Sheraton Waikiki, one poolside and one near the hotel entrance. Both are still open; when they opened isn't known yet.

name: The Cookie Corner
note: Shop in the Sheraton Waikiki lobby run by The Cookie Corner, a Honolulu cookie bakery founded in the early 1980s. It is still open, but when this shop opened has not been confirmed.

name: Royal Hawaiian Bakery
note: The Royal Hawaiian's press release and Honolulu Magazine report the bakery opened February 1, 2017; the release lists the resort address as 2259 Kalakaua Avenue.

name: Izakaya Pau Hana Base
note: Izakaya Pau Hana Base operates at 407 Seaside Ave (#107) in Waikiki and was open by at least 2017.

name: Sushi Sho
note: Honolulu Magazine reported in September 2016 that Sushi Sho had quietly opened at the Ritz-Carlton Residences Waikiki; Travelweek dates its opening to mid-September, and Ritz-Carlton confirms its current address.

name: La Vie
note: French-inspired fine dining restaurant on the lobby level of The Ritz-Carlton Residences, Waikiki Beach, which opened in 2019 in place of BLT Market. It was rebranded as Solera Waikiki in spring 2025.

name: Topped Waikiki
note: Topped Waikiki relocated from Kuhio Ave to 333 Royal Hawaiian Ave (Unit B) in May 2021.

name: Waikiki Market
note: Grocery store on the second floor of the Lilia Waikiki apartment tower, opened on January 11, 2023 on the former site of the Food Pantry store. It closed in spring 2026 for renovation and reopened that August.

name: Sushi Spot Waikiki
note: Sushi restaurant at the corner of Kuhio and Liliʻuokalani avenues, a Waikiki offshoot of the owner's earlier Sushi Spot in Aiea, open by about 2022. In 2025 it began serving brunch in the same space as Brunch Spot Waikiki.

name: Vive Hotel Waikiki
note: Boutique hotel on Kuhio Avenue that opened in mid-2013, with its guest rooms and suites on the upper floors above a parking garage.

name: Genius Lounge Japanese Sake Bar ＆ Dining
note: Genius Lounge Japanese Sake Bar & Dining opened in November 2009 at 346 Lewers St in Waikiki.

name: Skybox Taphouse
note: Skybox Taphouse opened on September 9, 2021 on the 3rd floor Grand Lanai of International Market Place (2330 Kalakaua Ave #302).

name: Mitsuwa Marketplace
note: The Japanese supermarket chain's first Hawaii store, which opened in May 2017 on the second level of International Market Place near Saks Fifth Avenue. Its food court was later remodeled and renamed The Japan.

name: Magnolia Ice Cream & Treats
note: Filipino-inspired ice cream shop on the second level of International Market Place, known for ube ice cream and halo-halo. The chain opened its first Hawaii scoop shop in Waipahu in 2015, and the year this Waikiki shop opened has not been confirmed.

name: Liliha
note: Liliha Bakery opened its Waikiki location on the 3rd floor Grand Lanai of International Market Place (2330 Kalakaua Ave) in November 2021.

name: Honolulu Cookie Company
note: Tabelog lists the Waikiki Beach Walk store at 227 Lewers St and records its opening in 2007; Honolulu Cookie Company's official history says several new Waikiki stores opened that year, and its current locator confirms the address.

name: Penny's Waikiki Malasadas
note: Malasada shop on the second level of Building B at Royal Hawaiian Center, the first storefront of a business that began as a food truck in Lāʻie in 2018. It opened at the center around 2021–2022.

name: Breakout Waikiki
note: Live-action escape room venue at Waikiki Beach Walk. It moved here from its first location at King's Village and held a grand re-opening in May 2019.

name: Honolulu Noodle & Co.
note: Taiwanese beef noodle shop in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It opened in early 2023 as the food hall launched.

name: Nori Bar
note: Aloha State Daily reports Nori Bar just opened its Waikiki location on Kūhiō Avenue in April 2026 and gives the contact address as 2255 Kūhiō Ave. The restaurant’s official site confirms the Waikiki location at that address; the task did not list one.

name: natuRe waikiki
note: natuRe waikiki is a sustainable Island French restaurant that opened December 17, 2021, on the second floor at 413 Seaside Avenue in Waikiki.

name: Waikiki Gun Club
note: The Hawaii Waikiki Gun Club, an indoor shooting range at 2142 Kalakaua Avenue, 2nd Floor, was established in 1988 and remains in operation at that address.

name: Aloha Greek
note: Aloha Greek Waikiki, a self-serve frozen Greek yogurt shop, opened in March 2026 at 2375 Kuhio Ave in Waikiki.

name: Honolulu Skewer House
note: Northern Chinese skewer restaurant that moved here from Makaloa Street, where it opened in 2018. It reopened in Unit 1A in December 2020, with grills at each table so diners cook their own skewers.

name: bb.q Chicken
note: bb.q Chicken opened its third Hawaii location, a Korean fried chicken restaurant, at 2250 Kalakaua Ave, Suite 114, in Waikiki Shopping Plaza in 2025.

name: Aloha Hot Dog & Banh Mi
note: Aloha Hot Dog & Banh Mi, a Vietnamese-Hawaiian fusion stall serving hot dogs on Hawaiian buns and banh mi sandwiches, opened in 2024 on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza at 2250 Kalakaua Ave, Unit LL105.

name: Waffle and Berry
note: Waffle and Berry, a locally owned waffle and acai bowl cafe established in 2019 at Ohana Hale Marketplace, opened at its current Waikiki Shopping Plaza location, 2250 Kalakaua Ave, Lower Level #104, in 2023.

name: Noa
note: Noa Botanicals (Noa), a medical cannabis dispensary, opened its Waikiki location at 345 Royal Hawaiian Avenue on April 19, 2025.

name: Sam's Kitchen Express
note: Takeout branch of the Waikiki plate-lunch restaurant Sam's Kitchen, known for garlic shrimp, in Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It opened around 2025 and is still open.

name: Allegrini Italian Deli & Market
note: Allegrini Mozzarella, an authentic Italian deli and market, opened at 2250 Kalakaua Ave in the Waikiki Shopping Plaza's lower level at the end of 2024, after previously operating in Downtown Honolulu.

name: Nana's Green Tea
note: Japanese matcha cafe that opened in December 2016 in the Waikiki Yokocho food alley, in the basement of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It was the chain's first U.S. location. It soft-opened again in the same space in January 2023 as part of the Stix Asia food hall.

name: Shanghai Bar
note: Cocktail bar with a 1930s Shanghai theme in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It was serving Asian-inspired cocktails and Japanese spirits by spring 2023.

name: Haleiwa Town Shave Ice
note: Haleiwa Town Shave Ice opened at the end of 2024 on the basement/lower level of the Waikiki Shopping Plaza at 2250 Kalakaua Ave, bringing North Shore-style shave ice to Waikiki.

name: Udon Yama
note: Udon Yama, a Japanese restaurant serving handmade Sanuki udon, opened in February 2023 as one of the original tenants of the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of the Waikiki Shopping Plaza at 2250 Kalakaua Ave.

name: Good Chicken
note: Korean fried chicken stall, a second location of the Kaka'ako shop, that soft-opened in March 2024 in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza.

name: Tanaka of Tokyo
note: The original Hawaii location of the Tanaka of Tokyo teppanyaki steakhouse, now called Tanaka of Tokyo Central, opened in Waikiki Shopping Plaza in 1978. It reportedly moved from the plaza's fourth floor to its third floor in 2012.

name: Honolulu Cookie Company
note: Company history dates the Waikiki Shopping Plaza store opening to 2020; its store locator identifies this address.

name: Sephora
note: Sephora opened its third Hawaii store, about 7,500 square feet, at Waikiki Shopping Plaza in September 2010.

name: Ribs & Broth
note: Vietnamese pho shop known for beef back rib pho, on the Noodle Street section of the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It opened around January 2024.

name: Ramen Baikohken
note: Waikiki branch of a Michelin-listed ramen shop from Asahikawa, Hokkaido. It opened in February 2017 in the Waikiki Yokocho food alley in the basement of Waikiki Shopping Plaza, then reopened in the same space when the STIX Asia food hall launched in 2023.

name: Sushi Matsuri
note: Sushi counter from Japan's Setouchi region serving nigiri and maki in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It was one of the 13 restaurants open at the food hall's grand opening on February 6, 2023.

name: Ao Gelato
note: Gelato shop run by Nana's Green Tea, making gelato with premium teas and tropical fruits. It was one of the original eateries at the February 2023 opening of the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza.

name: Tempura Kiki
note: Japanese tempura restaurant, also called Kiki Authentic Tempura, in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It opened in 2023 in the space formerly held by Tempura Kaneko Hannosuke.

name: Shingen
note: Japanese noodle shop known for fresh soba in the STIX ASIA food hall on the lower level of Waikiki Shopping Plaza. It was one of the restaurants open at the food hall's grand opening in February 2023.

name: Hilton Waikiki Beach
note: The former Prince Kuhio hotel, earlier run by Outrigger and then Radisson, officially became the Hilton Waikiki Prince Kuhio on April 5, 2007 after a $65 million renovation. It later took the Hilton Waikiki Beach name.

name: Hyatt Regency Waikiki Beach Resort and Spa
note: Large beachfront hotel with twin octagonal towers, built in 1976 by developer Chris Hemmeter on the site of the demolished Waikiki Biltmore Hotel. It still operates under the Hyatt Regency name.

name: OUTRIGGER Waikiki Beach Resort
note: Oceanfront Waikiki hotel established in 1967 on land that had been occupied by the Outrigger Canoe Club. It celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2017 and has 524 rooms.

name: Waikiki Resort Hotel
note: Nineteen-story hotel on Koa Avenue, built around 1970 and still operating. It had a major renovation in 2008.

name: Stay Hotel Waikiki
note: Hotel on Koa Avenue in a building that was long a dormitory for University of Hawaiʻi students. It opened as a budget hotel in 2011.

name: Ka Laʻi Waikiki Beach, LXR Hotels & Resorts
note: Luxury condo-hotel on Saratoga Road that joined Hilton's LXR Hotels & Resorts on February 7, 2024. It was previously the Trump International Hotel Waikiki, and its owners bought out the Trump licensing agreement before the rebrand.

name: 'Alohilani Resort Waikiki Beach
note: Oceanfront resort created from the former Pacific Beach Hotel through a $125 million transformation. It celebrated its grand opening on May 8, 2018.

name: Halepuna Waikiki by Halekulani
note: Sister hotel of the Halekulani, across the street from it, created by a year-long renovation of the former Waikiki Parc Hotel. It welcomed its first guests on October 25, 2019, closed during the 2020 pandemic and reopened on April 1, 2021.

name: La Piña Cantina
note: Mexican cantina serving margaritas, tequila and Mexican dishes in the Kūhiō Ave Food Hall on Level 1 of International Market Place. It was one of the hall's first two vendors when the hall opened in spring 2021.

name: Big Island Burger
note: Big Island Burger opened at the end of 2024 in Unit 102 of the Waikiki Shopping Plaza.

name: Secret Spot
note: Secret Spot Honolulu, a café-bar and live-music venue in Space A of The Laylow Waikiki, held its grand opening beginning June 17, 2024.

name: Hyatt Place Waikiki Beach
note: Hawaii's first Hyatt Place, created by renovating and rebranding the former Ocean Resort Hotel Waikiki. Its Pali Tower opened on December 8, 2011, and its Diamond Head Tower followed in April 2012.

name: Waikiki Beach Marriott Resort & Spa
note: Marriott bought the Hawaiian Regent Hotel, which opened in 1971, in November 2000 and renamed it the Waikiki Beach Marriott Resort. A $60 million renovation was finished in early 2002.

name: The Surfjack Hotel & Swim Club
note: Boutique hotel with 112 rooms in a midcentury style, which opened on March 31, 2016, in a renovated Lewers Street building from around 1960. Its pool deck hosts the Swim Club, and Ed Kenney's restaurant Mahina and Sun's is also inside.

name: Shoreline Hotel Waikiki
note: Boutique hotel with 135 rooms on Seaside Avenue, formerly the Seaside Hotel, once owned by United Airlines. It reopened as Shoreline Hotel Waikiki in spring 2013 after a renovation under Joie de Vivre Hotels.

name: OHANA Waikiki Malia
note: Kuhio Avenue hotel renamed from Waikiki Malia to OHANA Waikiki Malia in March 2000, when Outrigger put all its OHANA-brand hotels under that name. Outrigger used the OHANA name until about 2020, and by 2021 the hotel was called Waikiki Malia by Outrigger.

name: The Laylow Waikiki, Autograph Collection
note: Boutique hotel on Kuhio Avenue and Oahu's first Marriott Autograph Collection property. Its grand opening was announced in May 2017 after a renovation.

name: Waikiki Community Center
note: Nonprofit community center founded in 1978 that serves Waikiki seniors and children. It first operated at other Waikiki sites and moved to the former St. Augustine School grounds after the state bought them in 1981.

name: Denny's
note: Hawaii Lodging & Tourism Association's July 2018 archive reports attending the new Denny's grand opening at the Kuhio/Kapahulu intersection; Denny's current location directory confirms 208 Kapahulu Avenue.

name: Aston at the Waikiki Banyan
note: All-suite condominium hotel in the twin-tower Waikiki Banyan, a block from Waikiki Beach, now run by Aston. The towers date from the late 1970s, and the Aston name came later.

name: Cuckoo Coconuts Waikiki
note: Open-air tiki bar on Royal Hawaiian Avenue between Kalakaua and Kuhio avenues, known for nightly live music and tropical cocktails. A tiki-bar directory dates its opening to about 2014.

name: Wayfinder Waikiki
note: The hotel's site reports an initial opening January 9, 2023. A later announcement places the official grand opening in May 2023 at 2375 Ala Wai Boulevard.

name: Park Shore Waikiki
note: High-rise hotel at the Diamond Head end of Waikiki, across from Kapiolani Park and near the Honolulu Zoo, built around 1968. It still operates as a hotel.

name: Queen Kapiolani Hotel
note: The hotel's own history says it opened in 1969 and gives 150 Kapahulu Avenue as its address.

name: Aston Waikiki Beach Tower
note: All-suite condominium hotel in a tower across from Kuhio Beach, opened around 1984 and later run under the ResortQuest and Aston names. In 2018 it relaunched after a renovation as The Residences at Waikiki Beach Tower.

name: Royal Hawaiian Hotel
note: Beachfront hotel on Kalakaua Avenue that opened on February 1, 1927, according to the Historic Hawai‘i Foundation. It is still operating.

name: Waikiki Circle Hotel
note: Round, 14-story hotel across Kalakaua Avenue from Waikiki Beach, opened around 1962–1963 (the hotel itself gives 1963). It has operated under the Aston and Castle management brands.

name: Hilton Garden Inn Waikiki Beach
note: Hilton Garden Inn hotel on Kuhio Avenue across from International Market Place, opened in June 2016 as the brand's first property on Oahu. It took over and fully renovated the former Ohana Waikiki West hotel.

name: Moana Surfrider
note: Historic Hotels of America identifies this address and the original Moana Hotel opening on March 11, 1901. Moana Surfrider is its current name, so the year refers to the original hotel.

name: Sheraton Waikiki
note: Large beachfront hotel on Kalakaua Avenue that opened on June 4, 1971. After a renovation finished in 2023 it was renamed the Sheraton Waikiki Beach Resort.

name: Wyndham at Waikiki Beach Walk
note: Wyndham timeshare resort with 195 units in two towers, redeveloped from former Ohana hotel buildings during the Waikiki Beach Walk project and opened for guests in November 2006. It now operates as Club Wyndham at Waikiki Beach Walk.

name: Aloha Surf Hotel
note: Condo-hotel on Kanekapolei Street in a 15-story building completed around 1968. It still operates today as Aqua Aloha Surf Waikiki.

name: Romer House Waikiki
note: Adults-only hotel that opened June 1, 2024 after a $29 million renovation of a 1960 building, first built as the Royal Prince Apartment Building and later known as the Pearl Hotel. It was billed as Oahu's first adults-only hotel.

name: Waikiki Grand Hotel
note: Hotel across from the Honolulu Zoo, built around 1962–63 by developer Kanae Kobayashi to a design by architect Ernest Hara. It opened with 172 rooms at $7.50 to $24 a night and still operates as a condo-hotel.

name: Ilima Hotel
note: Family-owned condo-style hotel with 98 rooms on Nohonani Street, open since 1968 and still operating.

name: Hotel Renew
note: Boutique hotel with 72 rooms near the Diamond Head end of Waikiki. It opened in 2008 after a multimillion-dollar remodel of an older building, formerly the Ocean Tower Hotel, and Aston Hotels & Resorts took over running it in 2013.

name: Hokulani Waikiki by Hilton Grand Vacations
note: Hilton Grand Vacations timeshare resort at Kalakaua Avenue and Lewers Street, built in place of the former OHANA Islander Waikiki Hotel. It opened in December 2013 and held its grand opening in January 2014.

name: The Ritz-Carlton Residences, Waikiki Beach
note: Oahu's first Ritz-Carlton property, a luxury condo-hotel that opened in July 2016 with its 38-story first tower. Its second tower, the Diamond Head Tower, opened in October 2018 and completed the resort.

name: Embassy Suites by Hilton Waikiki Beach Walk
note: All-suite hotel that opened in December 2006 as the anchor of the Waikiki Beach Walk redevelopment. It was built on the site of the former Ohana Waikiki Village and Ohana Waikiki Tower hotels.

name: Waikiki Beach Walk
note: Outrigger's open-air shopping, dining and entertainment district on Lewers Street at Kalakaua Avenue, part of a major redevelopment of the street. A few tenants opened in late 2006, and the center opened in 2007.

name: Waikiki Shopping Plaza
note: Multi-story shopping, dining and office complex at the corner of Kalakaua and Seaside avenues, developed by William K.H. Mau and newly built in about 1977. It still houses shops and restaurants.

name: Outrigger Reef Waikiki Beach Resort
note: Beachfront hotel designed by Roy Kelley that opened in 1955 as the Reef Hotel, and later operated under the Outrigger name as the Outrigger Reef Waikiki Beach Resort.

name: White Sands Hotel
note: Low-rise hotel on Nohonani Street built in 1957, with its rooms set around a courtyard pool. It reopened in 2021 after a retro-style renovation and is still operating.

name: OHANA East Hotel
note: Hotel at Kuhio and Kaiulani Avenues, built around 1972 and first run as the Outrigger East. It became the OHANA East Hotel on December 1, 2001, later OHANA Waikiki East, and in October 2024 was renamed OUTRIGGER Waikiki Paradise Hotel after a renovation.

name: International Market Place
note: Open-air shopping and entertainment center founded by Donn Beach in 1956. Its original buildings were torn down in 2013, and the rebuilt center reopened on August 25, 2016.

name: Courtyard by Marriott Waikiki Beach
note: Marriott opened this Courtyard hotel with a Hawaiian blessing ceremony on June 2, 2009. The property was formerly The Wyland Waikiki, which had been renovated in 2007, in a building listed as built in 1969.

name: Kith
note: Kith's Hawaii flagship store opened August 20, 2021 at Royal Hawaiian Center.

name: Kith Treats
note: Dessert shop and cereal bar inside the Kith Hawaii flagship store, which opened August 20, 2021 at the Royal Hawaiian Center.

note: Open today (museum). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

note: Open today (gift). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: The Royal Hawaiian Theatre
note: A 750-seat theater on the fourth floor of Royal Hawaiian Center, opened around July 2008 as Level 4 for the Waikiki Nei show. Today it is the Royal Hawaiian Theater, home of the Rock-A-Hula show.

name: ABC
note: Open today (convenience). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: P.F. Chang's
note: Opened at Royal Hawaiian Center in March 2008. It reopened in September 2021 after a major renovation.

name: Dior
note: Open today (clothes). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: Victoria's Secret
note: Lingerie and clothing store at the corner of Kalākaua and Royal Hawaiian avenues. It held its grand opening on October 11, 2011, with model Alessandra Ambrosio, and is still open.

name: Lulu's Waikiki
note: Open-air restaurant and bar on the second floor of the Park Shore Waikiki hotel at Kalākaua and Kapahulu. It opened in November 2004 in the space Denny's had left earlier that year.

name: Waikiki Beachside Bistro
note: Open today (fast food). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: Island Vintage Coffee
note: Kona coffee cafe on the second floor of Royal Hawaiian Center, run by a brand that dates its start to 1996. This cafe was built in the newly renovated center and won a remodeling award in 2009, so it likely opened around 2008. Still open today.

name: Five-O Bar & Lounge
note: Bar and lounge that opened in August 2011 on the second floor of Royal Hawaiian Center, near the Paina Lanai food court, replacing the former Grove Bar. Still open today.

name: Eggs 'n Things Waikiki Beach Eggspress
note: A quick-service and takeout branch of the Waikiki breakfast chain, which started on Ena Road in 1974. It opened in late 2011 in the lobby of the Waikiki Circle Hotel.

note: Open today (convenience). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: La Cucaracha Waikiki
note: Open today (restaurant). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: Waikiki Brew Company
note: Brewpub that opened in 2015 at the corner of Kalakaua Ave and Ala Moana Blvd, Waikiki's first brewery. The company later moved its main brewing to Kakaako, and the Waikiki pub reopened after a full renovation in November 2020.

name: Mac 24/7 Bar & Restaurant
note: Opened around 2007 as the 24-hour signature restaurant of the Hilton Waikiki Prince Kuhio, after the hotel's $65 million renovation and switch to Hilton. The hotel is now Hilton Waikiki Beach.

name: Tiki's Meeting Spot
note: Tiki bar in the Ohia Waikiki Studio Suites building, renamed from Lava Tube around May 2025. It closed in April 2026 when its lease ended ahead of renovations.

name: TR Fire Grill
note: Opened in December 2016 inside the Hilton Garden Inn Waikiki Beach, as the chain's second restaurant and first franchise location. It took over the hotel's former Chili's space.

name: Marugame Udon
note: Self-serve udon restaurant that opened April 1, 2011 as Marukame Udon, the Japanese chain's first Hawaii location. It later took the name Marugame Udon.

name: Jamba
note: Open today (fast food). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: EbiNomi
note: Open today (restaurant). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: Kono's Northshore
note: Open today (fast food). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: Bank of Hawaii
note: Bank of Hawaii moved its Waikiki branch to the ground floor of this building, renamed the Bank of Hawaii Waikiki Center, around mid-2008. The branch had been at Kalakaua and Royal Hawaiian, and the ground-floor space was formerly the Wyland Gallery.

name: Henry's Place
note: Open today (fast food). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: Me's Bar-B-Que
note: Open today (restaurant). Listed in OpenStreetMap; the year it opened isn't known yet.

name: Bacchus Waikiki
note: Second-floor gay bar on Lewers Street at Kuhio Avenue. It held its grand opening party in August 2011.

name: Surf N Turf Tacos
